A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, equations, references, and complete appendices. V2 Appendices A–D correspond to v3 Appendices B–E; v3 adds a new Appendix A.

before.justification: V2 reports original training experiments, accuracy measurements, mechanistic introspection, and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains original small-transformer experiments and adds language-model counting evaluations and alphabet-size, sequence-length, and depth experiments in Appendices A and E.

M1.justification: Appendix E.8 introduces a two-block architectural extension with independently parameterized attention/feed-forward stages, retaining the same embedding and hidden dimensions. This changes the computation of an added model variant. The original one-block architectures and relation-based and inventory-based counting constructions remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 adds English prompted counting over letters, animal names, and months, using both positional and semantic queries (Appendix A), substantially extending the synthetic per-token histogram evaluations. It also tests sequence lengths 5, 15, and 30, beyond the length-10 experiments in v2. Alphabet size 64 was already represented in v2’s illustrative experiments.

E2.justification: The small-model comparisons retain lin, dot, and bos, each with and without softmax. The added sweeps and depth experiments reuse these families. Mistral and Llama are evaluated separately in Appendix A, rather than introduced as baselines in the small-model comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 introduces an LLM evaluation protocol with 100 ten-item lists per sampling strategy, four prompt formulations, and temperature-zero predictions. It adds alphabet-size, sequence-length, and depth sweeps and changes configurations in retained introspection examples. The main small-model training protocol remains 500 epochs, 10,000 fresh samples per epoch, and 3,000 evaluation samples.

E4.justification: Appendices E.6–E.8 add systematic alphabet-size and sequence-length sensitivity analyses and a one-versus-two-layer comparison, testing the generality and limitations of the learning regimes. Appendix A also examines sensitivity to query formulation and item category. The earlier frozen-embedding, BOS intervention, and singular-value analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs for the principal architecture sweep and frozen-embedding experiments, with mean accuracies and a supplementary standard-deviation analysis. V3 does not introduce a different repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice; the LLM list counts describe evaluation sample sizes.

E6.justification: V3 adds LLM confusion matrices and alphabet-size, sequence-length, and depth results, including deteriorated learning at length 30 and generally better two-layer performance. It also replaces illustrative results: lin+sftm changes from 99.97% at T=64, p=d=128 in v2 Figure 5 to 100% at T=32, p=d=64 in v3 Figure 4, both with L=10. These different configurations do not establish a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Propositions 4.1–4.5, the inventory-counting appendix proposition, mutual-coherence derivations, softmax constructions, and d=4 remark are retained. Matching v2 Appendices A–B against v3 Appendices B–C reveals renumbering and typographical changes, without substantive mathematical revisions. The two-layer extension has no new theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The central claims about two counting strategies, architectural dependence, and robustness to non-orthogonal embeddings remain. V3’s introduction and conclusion additionally assert counting failures in the tested 7–8B language models and empirical transfer of learning regimes to two-layer models, modestly broadening the claimed scope.

C2.justification: V3 interprets length-30 failures as possible optimization difficulties under a fixed training budget and hypothesizes that an extra layer assists optimization and robustness. Appendix E.8 explicitly qualifies the depth findings as exploratory and unsupported by theory beyond one layer. Existing applicability and finite-precision limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A documents LLM checkpoints, Torch/float16 use, exact prompts, item lists, and sampling procedures. Appendix E.8 specifies parameter independence and residual structure for the added architecture. The public repository address remains available, although the softmax-construction appendix replaces its local URL with the generic phrase 'supplementary material'.

R1.justification: V3 adds Golkar et al., Nichani et al., and discussion of concurrent counting work by Yehudai et al., including its treatment of numerical precision and bounds. The LLM evaluations introduce Mistral and Llama references. The broader research positioning remains stable; publication and bibliographic updates to retained works are not new citations.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets are substantially rewritten, background and experimental descriptions are condensed, and related work and the conclusion receive extensive editing. A new Section 4.3 summarizes expanded experiments, and the LLM appendix precedes the renumbered existing appendices. These changes substantially revise the paper’s exposition.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, rearranges Figure 1’s panels, merges the inventory-counting figures into Figure 4, and redraws the entangled-embedding illustration with revised axes and examples. It adds LLM confusion-matrix figures and seven alphabet-size, sequence-length, and depth figures, while retaining and relocating earlier appendix displays.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens empirical validation of the central learning-regime claims beyond v2’s predominantly fixed-length, one-layer experiments. The alphabet-size, sequence-length, and depth analyses both support broader applicability and expose the length-30 optimization failure, making the claims’ practical boundaries clearer. The original theoretical foundation is preserved, while Appendix E.8 appropriately acknowledges that the two-layer findings remain exploratory.
